messages:
sam (Support): Hi team — customer reporting intermittent 401s in the Console when saving model rollout rules. They see it in Edge and Chrome. Request ID shown in UI: r-0a1b2c3d. Asking for HAR + console so we can repro.

maria (Support): Thanks Sam. Can you ask them to include the full devtools export (Network HAR) *and* the console log? We need the request headers and the JSON response body with the X-Request-ID.

sam (Support): Yep sent steps below to customer. Pasting here so eng-sre can review if anything else needed: 
- Reproduce in an incognito window (to avoid extensions)
- Open DevTools (F12) -> Network tab
- Check "Preserve log" and "Disable cache"
- Click the red record dot if not recording
- Reproduce the auth failure in the Console UI (save rollout rule)
- Right-click any request -> "Save all as HAR with content" -> attach file
- Switch to Console tab -> right-click -> "Save as..." -> attach console log

devon (Eng-SRE): Good. Add: in Network -> find the failing request (status 401) and right-click -> "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL (bash)" and paste it here or attach. That gives us exact headers + body. Also ask customer to expand the Response body in the network panel and include a screenshot if they can't export bodies.

sam (Support): Also requested that they grab the request headers and look for these headers: Authorization, x-request-id (or x-rw-request-id), content-type, and any cookie. If they see a 401 response with an error JSON, include the full JSON.

maria (Support): If they're on Edge, note: Edge devtools flow is identical to Chrome but sometimes the context menu labels differ — "Save all as HAR" is present. For Firefox: Network tab -> right-click -> "Save all as HAR" as well.

devon (Eng-SRE): Add troubleshooting tips we want them to try if capture is hard: 
- Try reproducing with a plain curl using the cURL copy. Run: 
  curl --location --request POST 'https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/rollouts' \n  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  --data-raw '{"name":"test","rules":...}'
- Replace token with the one from the failing request header. If curl returns 401, paste the error and the complete request-id header from the response.

sam (Support): Customer asked how to get the console messages with preserved timestamps. I told them: In Console -> click the kebab menu (•••) -> "Preserve log" and then reproduce, then right-click -> "Save as...". If they prefer, they can select all and copy/paste into a .txt file.

maria (Support): Please remind customer to remove any PII or secrets before upload (do not paste full tokens in public tickets). They can redact the Authorization header except keep the first 6 chars and last 4 for debugging, and keep the x-request-id intact.

devon (Eng-SRE): If they can't export HAR due to corporate policy, ask for: the copied cURL, screenshot of network panel showing request + response headers, and full console log. That is usually enough to diagnose.

sam (Support): I've asked them to upload to our secure support drop: https://redwood.support/upload (internal link) and to include the ticket number.

maria (Support): One more useful capture: in Network -> right-click failing request -> "Copy" -> "Copy Response". That gives the raw JSON body. Helpful if HAR scrubs bodies.

sam (Support): Customer replied they reproduced and attached a file but they couldn't get response bodies included. Asked if we can enable any special setting.

devon (Eng-SRE): If bodies are missing, tell them to ensure "Preserve log" is on and that they choose "Save all as HAR with content" (not just HAR). In Chrome, sometimes third-party cookie policies strip authorization during incognito; have them try a normal profile with only required auth cookie present.

maria (Support): I'll follow up asking them to re-run with the "with content" option and to paste the cURL here if still missing.

support-bot: Uploaded support bundle received for ticket #12345 — processing. :white_check_mark:

sam (Support): Thanks — once we have the HAR + console + cURL we'll triage and escalate to eng-runtime if we reproduce a server-side 401. If it's a client-side token refresh issue we'll note that in the ticket.

devon (Eng-SRE): Also asking Eng-Runtime to grep logs for the x-request-id r-0a1b2c3d around the timestamp the customer reported. That will confirm whether the backend returned 401 or if something got dropped in the gateway.

maria (Support): Great — I'll keep the customer updated. :thumbsup:
